notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated GPU pools across NA/EU with multi-AZ failover headroom. Goal is hard throughput guarantees for trade‑support chat and reranking plus tight p95 latency SLOs for front‑end flows.

Context + ask: Hightower runs low-latency trade desk assistants (chat) and real‑time reranking for trade flows. They need predictable token throughput during market open windows (spikes), cross‑region failover that preserves latency SLOs, and clear SLA language for latency/availability. Procurement asked for a capacity plan they can attach to an SOW.

Requirements (from architecture + infra leads):
- Throughput targets: sustain 600 concurrent chat streams at ~10 tokens/sec average (steady load), peak 2,400 concurrent streams for 5–10 minutes (market open).
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms for short-form chat (<=512 tokens), worst-case fallback p95 < 400ms.
- Embeddings / batch scoring: 20k vectors/hr baseline, bursts to 80k/hr during end-of-day windows.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to 12–24 month reserved capacity if unit costs reduce by >=30% vs on-demand.
- Deployment: primary NA region (us-east), second region EU (eu-west) as active standby with warm pool. On‑prem fallback for compliance-bound segments.

POC results (summary of tests run 2026-02/03):
- Stress test ff_20260302_stress-test: 6x A100-80GB equivalent (dedicated pool) with optimized batching and KV caching handled ~85 req/s for canonical chat template with p95 ≈ 210ms.
- Multi-AZ failover run: simulated AZ outage in us-east; automatic routing to warm instances in us-east-b with ~3s reconnection jitter, p95 rose to ~360ms until prefix cache warmed.
- EU cold-warm test: cross-region failover to eu-west (warm pool at 40% capacity) added 70–120ms RTT; observed p95 ≈ 330–420ms depending on token length and model variant.

Preliminary reserved GPU pool plan (proposal outline sent to customer):
- us-east (primary, production): reserve pool = 32 x H100-equivalent GPUs. Headroom: 30% spare (9 GPUs) for AZ failover and burst. Provision across 3 AZs: 12 / 12 / 8 distribution to reduce single-AZ blast radius.
- eu-west (active-standby): reserve pool = 12 x H100-equivalent GPUs. Warmed to 40% (active routes for geo‑localized traffic). Headroom: 25% for cross-region failover.
- on-prem (regulatory subset): 6 x A100-80GB on dedicated racks for PII-sensitive request routing; used for data residency, not full global failover.
- Burst capacity option: allow 10% burstable GPUs in shared zone for short market spikes, billed at higher rate but guaranteed >= 5 minutes provisioning.

Why these numbers: back-of-envelope based on POC throughput, per‑GPU sustained concurrency (~18–22 chat streams per GPU at target latency with batching and KV cache), plus 30% headroom for AZ failover and cache warmup. EU pool sized to cover regional traffic + emergency cross-region failover with degraded latency acceptable per compliance.

SLA negotiation points flagged by legal/procurement:
- Precise latency measurement methodology (client observed vs server token end-to-end).
- How fallback to smaller/quantized model variants affects SLA credits.
- Scheduled maintenance windows and how they impact multi-region redundancy guarantees.
- Credits for partial degradations (p95 violations) vs full outage.
- Data residency proof points for on-prem segments and audit log retention windows.

Open technical questions (needs SE + infra doc):
- Cache reconciliation after cross-region failover: timeline to rehydrate prefix/KV cache and options for controlled pre-warming.
- Network egress allocation model in mixed VPC/on‑prem flows — want a clean chargeback template.
- Concrete per-token cost table for reserved + burst GPUs in each region for 12 vs 24 month terms.
